purpose: Four dark mature native UI concepts; user clarified UE4-era professional tool character, no themed decoration

concepts.title: Classic Workbench
concepts.direction: Closest to the strong UE4-era desktop character. A substantial graphite-gray toolbar spans the top of a darker near-black window, purple Q logo and modest Projects title at left; two substantial icon-and-label command buttons at right. The Open project button has a recognizable shaded neutral-gray folder symbol, New project has a solid small plus on a purple document symbol. Below, a deeply inset broad project list in a firm dark frame with clearly raised column headers, precise separator rules and comfortable 60px rows. First row uses a subdued dark amber/brown selection fill and a thin warm focus edge, all surfaces remain dark. The list takes about 65% of screen height, with just a small empty dark area below four rows. Two low horizontal tutorial/docs panels below look like part of the same native tool window, with modest images and obvious raised rectangular action buttons. Clean crisp pixels, no textures. Strong tonal contrast between toolbar, header, rows and frame. The result should immediately recall the solidity of UE4's older Slate UI, adapted to Quader.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a convincing native Windows desktop application screenshot for Quader's project-list window, 16:10 landscape, front-on, crisp at high resolution. This is a professional level-design tool. ART DIRECTION: the confident substantial UI character of UNREAL ENGINE 4's Slate editor circa 2014–2020, before the flatter Unreal Engine 5 redesign. Visually serious, practical, bold, recognizable, compact. Dark gray raised toolbar faces, darker recessed content areas, tangible one-pixel highlights and shadows, clear strong panel hierarchy, conventional legible UI typography, distinctive professionally drawn tool icons with a little dimension. All backgrounds and control faces are DARK. Brighter text and a small selection accent are enough.
The supplied Quader screenshot is a reference for branding and FUNCTIONAL CONTENT ONLY. Preserve the purple geometric Q logo shape and existing functions, but reinterpret its surface hierarchy, control weight, panel proportions and toolbar composition.
The word "rock" in the user's brief means the confidence and character of old Unreal Editor. It MUST NOT cause ANY music, grunge, punk, poster, band, retro-rock, torn paper, rough type or distressed imagery. NO texture or material simulation. This must look like real serious native software.
Content: a modest Quader brand area and "Projects"; only two primary actions "Open project…" and "New project"; "Recent projects"; a table/list with "Project", "Last modified", "Editor version". Four project rows:

First row selected, last row muted. Every row ends in a small overflow ellipsis; consistent simple project-file icons, NOT project previews. Names bold, secondary paths smaller, aligned metadata. Replace the reference screenshot's old Size column with Editor version and relative dates.
Keep the two resource links "Your first hour in Quader" with "Start tutorial", and "Read the Docs" with "Open docs"; small muted dark grayscale architectural artwork may support these resources, but not dominate the screen. These links may be reorganized according to the direction below.
No extra features, search, filters, tabs for nonexistent pages, command catalogs, settings, account, console, status log, project preview inspector, invented text or slogans.
Must look plausible to implement in native Qt widgets. Normal system-font text, mostly 13–16px apparent size, compact 30–40px control heights. Quader/Projects heading no larger than 30–36px; no enormous wordmark. Use filled shaped file/folder/plus icons rather than exclusively hairline-outline icons. Corners mainly square with small 2–3px radii; tasteful subtle UI relief allowed, never glossy 3D.
ABSOLUTE AVOID: light theme, white or cream panels, bright large fills, magazine/poster layouts, grunge, paper, scratches, neon, glow, chrome, futuristic geometric fonts, chamfered sci-fi frames, spaceship UI, game main menu, clown aesthetics, generic SaaS cards and pill controls, oversized typography, broad empty margins, busy decorative patterns. This is Quader; no Unreal logos, name or copied proprietary icons.

concepts.title: Quader Studio
concepts.direction: A distinctly Quader interpretation of mature UE4-era software. A slim title band and strong charcoal action strip give a compact upper silhouette. A small purple Q emblem and clean bold QUADER wordmark, followed by Projects, all modest in size. Main Open/New commands use old-school professionally shaded tool icons and short bold labels in raised dark buttons. The recent-project table occupies three quarters of width. A narrow integrated right panel separated by a thick dark splitter contains the existing tutorial and documentation resources stacked, each with a small dim architectural image and clear button. Project rows use chunky neutral file icons, strong white names, restrained secondary paths. First selected row is a solid muted plum-gray band with a thin Quader-purple leading stripe, no glow. Header faces are visibly lighter charcoal than table body; black gutters reinforce hierarchy. No rounded floating cards. Serious, confident native app composition, no oversized branding.

concepts.title: Compact Workshop
concepts.direction: A compact workmanlike dark desktop tool with the proportions of classic game-development software. An integrated masthead has the small Q logo and Projects on the left and a short row of two closely grouped raised Open project/New project commands beside it; no large empty hero area. Strong dark-gray section title bar spans the full-width list. Table rows are approximately 52px tall, with compact bold names above paths; subtle alternating near-black and charcoal row surfaces, precise vertical column separators, traditional compact scrollbar. Selected first row is slightly lighter graphite with a 3px muted copper leading edge. Use mid-gray raised header faces and almost-black content fields, carefully lit one-pixel edges, restrained normal Segoe-like text. Tutorial/docs form two compact native information panes directly below the table with narrow horizontal artwork strips and actions aligned in a consistent baseline. This is the densest, most utilitarian variant: powerful clarity and deliberate control sizing, no ornament, no additional controls or status bar.

concepts.title: Slate Desktop
concepts.direction: A bold dark native launcher emphasizing integrated panel structure. Dark slate-gray outer window, near-black inset main list, a charcoal upper brand/action bar with modest Q logo and Projects at left, Open/New actions at right. A strong squared 'Recent projects' section header visually attaches to the content beneath, almost like a classic editor dock title but no invented tabs. Modestly larger 18px bold project names, crisp standard UI font; paths and metadata 13px; 62px horizontal rows. Selected first row is restrained deep blue-gray with a thin neutral light-gray edge and a small muted-purple file icon. Deep near-black separators and subtle one-pixel relief distinguish column headers from rows. Tutorial/docs are two short flat panes across the bottom with dark title strips, faint architecture imagery and visibly raised dark buttons. The emphasis is the silhouette and hierarchy of the panels: compact, durable, substantial. No trendy minimalism, no futuristic features, no texture. Professional and unmistakably a tool for creating worlds.
